snapshot.text: Health system pursuing universal health coverage, with the Ministry of Health aiming for a digital, primary-care-focused reform. Main challenges include recurrent medicine shortages at the Central Pharmacy and pressure on social funds. Notable now: a National Charter for Health signed in October 2026.

priorities.title: Central Pharmacy medicine supply overhaul
priorities.text: Cabinet approved urgent funding for the Central Pharmacy, digital tracking of drug supplies, faster drug marketing approvals and expanded local generic production to end shortages.

priorities.title: National Charter for Health, universal coverage
priorities.text: The ministry signed a charter with Japan, WHO and the World Bank to support universal health coverage; commitments go to a Tokyo summit in December 2026.

priorities.title: Digital health and sovereign health data
priorities.text: Plans include extending high-speed internet to primary care facilities, moving health data to Tunisian cloud solutions, using AI for analysis and creating a citizen digital call centre.

netherlands.text: A 2014 triangular programme, signed by the Dutch minister with a Tunisian counterpart, addressed maternal mortality and family planning in Mali and Yemen.
